svg.title: Libre DevOps container images: build, release and refresh flow
svg.text: Libre DevOps container images: build, release and refresh flow

versions.yml is the single source of truth. Every change reaches the registries through a pull request that builds, tests and scans every image on amd64 and arm64, and a published image is rebuilt as soon as a fix exists. Only a change made by hand waits for a person.

Renovate sees a new release of a tool, an agent or an image's main version, and bumps it in versions.yml: weekly, and at once for a security fix.
Every day the Pins workflow re-resolves each base image tag to its current digest, the newest Terraform providers, and every role in the Galaxy namespaces cicd-helper carries.
Renovate opens a pull request with the bump.

The Pins workflow pins every new download by SHA-256, locks Python dependencies by hash with any vulnerable one raised to its fix, and opens or updates its pull request. It does the same on every branch here that changes versions.yml.
Build runs on every push: every image and version, from one Containerfile, built natively on amd64 and arm64.
Each image's smoke tests run as uid 10001, as an arbitrary uid, and against a CA added at run time.
Trivy scans each image: any critical finding, or any high one with a fix, fails it, unless a VEX statement records why it does not apply.
Any failure blocks the pull request. The fix goes into the same pull request, which builds again.
When everything passes, a bot's pull request merges itself; a change made by hand waits for review.
Merging to main starts the Release workflow, which also runs every Monday.
Release builds every image again and pushes one digest per platform to both registries, with version, date and moving tags.
Every digest gets a cosign keyless signature, an SBOM and SLSA provenance.
Release records the new digests in README.md and releases.json, in a pull request that merges itself.
CI jobs, self-hosted agents, workstations and clusters pull from either registry, by tag or by digest, and can verify the signature first.
Every day the Scan workflow scans every published image again and reports findings in the Security tab. When a rebuild would fix one, it starts Release.
